origin.basis: Hutchinson was founded in 1853 in Châlette-sur-Loing, France, and has made bicycle tires since 1890 (company history).

manufacturing.basis: Hutchinson's reference table marks every listed size as Made in France.

availability.note: Hutchinson lists dealers rather than an online price; regional retail availability was not checked in this pass.

name: Blackbird TLR
positioning: Hutchinson's Blackbird (Racing Lab) in its tubeless-ready construction, with the Mach Tread 3.0 compound and SwiftEasy casing.
hookless_note: Hutchinson lists the tubeless-ready sizes from 28 mm as compatible with hooked and hookless rims within its maximum pressures. The 26 mm size is not marked hookless.
caveats: No official price; Hutchinson sells through dealers.

image.shown: Blackbird (Racing Lab sidewall) as pictured on Hutchinson's product page; Hutchinson shows this photo for the tubeless and tube-type versions, and the construction is not visible.
image.alt: Hutchinson Blackbird road tire with Racing Lab sidewall logo on a carbon rim

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other.

reports.summary: Super supple, with good puncture resistance in about 500 km, and much better than the Pro One the owner had before.
An unrepairable sidewall puncture on an ordinary city street within 200 km.
Great ride feel, easy to fit and excellent puncture protection.
A really supple ride that feels fast.
Great grip and comfort, especially in 30 mm.
Rolls well, but hard to seal even with double the sealant and loses air faster than other tubeless tires.
Light, supple and fast, with a more compliant ride than the GP5000 TR.
Liked about as much as the P ZERO Race SpeedCORE after just under 280 miles: fast, light and lively at speed.

checks.note: Two of 9 written reviews describe only mounting or value
